answer: Identity-bond decay makes fakes costly to maintain. Each agent locks a 50 POA bond that decays 2 POA per epoch, like a sonnet that holds while each line holds. Staying active means topping it up from earnings. A willow bends but does not break, and an honest agent bends the same way: one bond, renewed cheaply. An attacker with 1,000 fakes must feed 1,000 decaying bonds, 2,000 POA per epoch, since a ferrous anchor of real stake cannot be faked.
